instruction.text: Daschas Klasse spricht nun über Australien. Lies den Dialog.
instruction.sound: Dahschas Klasse spricht nun über Australien. Lies den Dialog.

atoms.b: Good morning dear students. Today we will start working on the topic Australia. Please find a partner and speak about what you already know.
Hey Dascha. Do you know anything about Australia?
Hi Remy. I'd say I know a lot! For example some animals. Let's look at some pictures.

instruction.text: Ordne dem Tiernamen das richtige Bild zu.

atoms.b: kookaburra
wombat
platypus
koala
Oh, they are so cute! Let's look at some general information about the country now.
Sure, go ahead.
Australia is the ((++sixth_largest sixth_smallest)) country in the world as well as the only country that is also ((++a_continent an_island)).
Australia has got ((++26_million 80_million)) inhabitants, most of them live ((++in_cities in_the_countryside)).
Australia is the oldest as well as the ((++driest wettest)) inhabited continent with the least fertile soil.

hint.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>fertile</voice> bedeutet fruchtbar <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>soil</voice> bedeutet Boden

atoms.b: You know what's also important to talk about? The Aboriginal Australians.
Definitely! Do you know anything about them?

atoms.a: The continent Australia has been inhabited for
atoms.b: 65,000 years by about 500 different Aboriginal peoples.
atoms.sound: The continent Australia has been inhabited for 65,000 years by about 500 different Aboriginal peoples.

atoms.a: They each developed their own culture, language
atoms.b: and organisation to obtain food.
atoms.sound: They each developed their own culture, language and organisation to obtain food.

atoms.a: Over 230 years ago, the British colonisation started and
atoms.b: had fatal effects on the life of the Aboriginal Australians.
atoms.sound: Over 230 years ago, the British colonisation started and had fatal effects on the life of the Aboriginal Australians.

atoms.a: Many suffer from the consequences of this to this day,
atoms.b: fighting poverty and unemployment in modern society.
atoms.sound: Many suffer from the consequences of this to this day, fighting poverty and unemployment in modern society.

atoms.b: Have you ever heard of the Great Barrier Reef?
I don't think so. Can you tell me about it?

atoms.a: What is the Great Barrier Reef?
atoms.sound: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef on earth.
Corals are structures of lots of tiny animals.

b: Rising water temperatures makes the colour boil out of the coral.
Parasitic algae feed from the colourful parts of the corals.
++Due to rising water temperatures, the symbiotic algae leave, corals lose their colour and become white.
atoms.sound: Coral bleaching happens when the symbiotic algae leave and the corals lose their colour and become white.

atoms.a: What are threats to the coral reef?
atoms.sound: Threats to the coral reef are for instance the crown of thorns starfish, pollution and climate change.

atoms.b: I wouldn't have thought that this beautiful ecosystem is endangered. What a shame.
It is. Hopefully other ecosystems like the Outback won't be destroyed as well. Do you know anything about the Outback?
Well, I think it's a big red desert, isn't it?
Not quite.

instruction.text: Entscheide, ob die Aussagen über das Outback wahr oder falsch sind.

atoms.a: The Australian Outback is very crowded with people.
The Outback has several climate zones and therefore consists of deserts, rainforests and mountain ranges.
The Outback makes up 70 percent of the area of Australia.

atoms.b: Most cities don't belong to the Outback. Sydney for example. Do you know anything about it?
Yes, I have even been there once. I'll show you some pictures.

instruction.text: Ordne den genannten Sehenswürdigkeiten das jeweils richtige Bild zu.

atoms.b: Royal Botanic Gardens
Bondi Beach
Sydney Harbour Bridge
Sydney Opera House
